            text: Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal

          issue:
            issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045
            title: 'Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
              under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive
              the acquisition'
            why_it_matters: ''
            parent_issue_id: null
            fact_ids: []
          facts:
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-182bcc
            text: Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
              weeks out).
            source_ids: &id003
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-551367
            text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance and full access to Mosaic's product set.
            source_ids: &id004
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9a0c61
            text: Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC'd by Harbor.
            source_ids: &id005
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-33293c
            text: Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
              Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.
            source_ids: &id006
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-aea8ec
            text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
              has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
              for users onboarded before 2023.
            source_ids: &id007
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-073838
            text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor's transaction feed at
              Mosaic's engine on day 1.
            source_ids: &id008
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-19aebc
            text: Marketing wants a 'Welcome' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
              launching close+1.
            source_ids: &id009
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-adf2cb
            text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.
            source_ids: &id010
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-4c1fd8
            text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance.
            source_ids: &id011
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f2c49f
            text: Plan is no re-verification of Harbor's existing KYC; Harbor users
              were already KYC'd.
            source_ids: &id012
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-13d4c1
            text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
              results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for
              users onboarded before 2023.
            source_ids: &id013
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-78d5cd
            text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
              Relay's engine on day 1.
            source_ids: &id014
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9f7bde
            text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.
            source_ids: &id015
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-ed9f06
            text: How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
              buys Harbor's assets)
            source_ids: &id016
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-b5e71e
            text: Does Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program currently permit relying on
              another institution's prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
              required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance
            source_ids: &id017
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-849b00
            text: What is known about Harbor's ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence
            source_ids: &id018
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f0fb01
            text: For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
              Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor's existing licenses or apply
              for its own? — Use/assume Harbor's licenses
            source_ids: &id019
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-620c62
            text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
              what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
              Relay's AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance
              must confirm.
            source_ids: &id020
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-070aec
            text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
              been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
              have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.
            source_ids: &id021
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-771ee1
            text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
              what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
              before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to
              use or assume Harbor's licenses for the four new markets.
            source_ids: &id022
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          assumptions:
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-29b823
            text: Mosaic Relay's existing money transmission licenses and Harbor's
              MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition without
              new state approval
            reason: Needed to continue
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-3c5756
            text: The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay's
              own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents
            reason: Needed to continue
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-1a519f
            text: The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and validated
              before close without a monitoring gap
            reason: Needed to continue
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-ca7dfd
            text: Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state MTL
              regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).
            reason: Needed to continue
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-d40239
            text: Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states
              (per the request).
            reason: Needed to continue
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-57e86b
            text: The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase, which
              affects whether Harbor's licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).
            reason: Needed to continue
          questions:
          - question_id: Q-SAR
            text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
              been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
            consequence: Unread open alerts and SARs are the highest-risk item; they
              can create BSA/AML exposure that must be addressed before close and
              could affect the deal itself.
            state: answered
            answer: The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain
              in diligence.
            answer_kind: reported_fact
            linked_fact_ids: &id023
            - FACT-20260909-070aec
          - question_id: Q-KYC
            text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
              what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations?
            consequence: Whether the missing underlying documents create a compliance
              gap depends on how Mosaic plans to satisfy its own CIP/recordkeeping
              obligations for these users.
            state: answered
            answer: It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program permits
              reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must confirm.
            answer_kind: reported_fact
            linked_fact_ids: &id024
            - FACT-20260909-620c62
          - question_id: Q-MTL
            text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
              what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
              before onboarding those customers?
            consequence: Whether the four new markets can be served at close depends
              on license transferability and state approval, which is a gating regulatory
              question.
            state: answered
            answer: Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor's licenses
              for the four new markets.
            answer_kind: reported_fact
            linked_fact_ids: &id025
            - FACT-20260909-771ee1
          - question_id: Q-BONUS
            text: How is the $50 welcome bonus structured?
            consequence: The structure determines whether the bonus triggers consumer
              disclosure, funds-flow, or state promotional requirements.
            state: left_open

              "content": "## Working position\n\nThe Harbor Pay migration needs legal
              and compliance review before the planned close. The leading concern
              is that an asset purchase generally requires Mosaic Relay to confirm
              its own authority to operate in each state; the current plan to use
              or assume Harbor''s licenses is not established as legally effective.\n\nThe
              second concern is BSA/AML readiness. Mosaic Relay has not confirmed
              whether its AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC,
              and underlying records are missing for some pre-2023 users. Harbor''s
              open alerts and SAR history also remain unread. These gaps make a day-one
              migration without re-verification or account restrictions difficult
              to support.\n\nTransaction monitoring continuity is also material because
              Harbor''s vendor ends at close. The repointed feed should be tested
              and validated before migrated users receive full access. The $50 bonus
              is lower priority but still needs review once its eligibility, funding,
              terms, and disclosures are known.\n\n## Plausible alternatives\n\nA
              narrower launch could exclude the four new markets, restrict users whose
              KYC evidence is incomplete, or delay full product access until alert
              review and monitoring validation finish. A full day-one launch remains
              possible only if state licensing, AML/CIP reliance, alert handling,
              and monitoring continuity are confirmed.\n\n## Material facts and assumptions\n\nReported
              facts include the asset-purchase structure, the current plan to rely
              on Harbor''s licenses, the lack of a compliance answer on KYC reliance,
              and the unread alerts and SAR history. The analysis assumes both entities
              conduct regulated money-transmission activity and that Mosaic Relay
              will become the operating provider immediately after close. It does
              not assume that Harbor''s licenses transfer or that Harbor''s KYC is
              sufficient.\n\n## What could change this view\n\nThe view could change
              if state counsel confirms an effective licensing path for each affected
              state, compliance confirms permissible reliance with adequate records
              or remediation, diligence clears the alerts and SAR history, and testing
              shows no monitoring gap. The bonus structure remains unknown.\n\n##
              Support limit\n\nThis is generated analysis based on reported matter
              facts. No external authority was retrieved.", "current_version_id":
              "REC-20260909-7112e7", "current_version_number": 1, "versions": [{"version_id":
              "REC-20260909-7112e7", "number": 1, "content": "## Working position\n\nThe
              Harbor Pay migration needs legal and compliance review before the planned

              Mosaic Relay to confirm its own authority to operate in each state;

              as legally effective.\n\nThe second concern is BSA/AML readiness. Mosaic
              Relay has not confirmed whether its AML/CIP program permits reliance
              on Harbor''s prior KYC, and underlying records are missing for some

              These gaps make a day-one migration without re-verification or account

              is also material because Harbor''s vendor ends at close. The repointed

              alternatives\n\nA narrower launch could exclude the four new markets,

              and assumptions\n\nReported facts include the asset-purchase structure,
              the current plan to rely on Harbor''s licenses, the lack of a compliance

              assumes both entities conduct regulated money-transmission activity
              and that Mosaic Relay will become the operating provider immediately

              history, and testing shows no monitoring gap. The bonus structure remains
              unknown.\n\n## Support limit\n\nThis is generated analysis based on

              "number": 2, "content": "**No external authority retrieved**\n\n## Practical
              answer\n\n**Do not treat Harbor’s 38 money transmitter licenses as transferable
              assets.** For closing purposes, assume that Mosaic cannot use them unless
              each relevant state regulator confirms a lawful path.\n\nAn asset purchase
              usually leaves the license with the licensed seller. It does not automatically
              move the license to the buyer. The buyer generally needs its own authority
              before it conducts regulated money transmission. A contract that says
              Mosaic “assumes” the licenses does not bind a regulator.\n\nThis makes
              the proposed four-state expansion a closing issue. It may also affect
              Harbor customers in states where both companies already hold licenses
              because the operating entity, customer agreement, custody of funds,
              or licensed activity can change.\n\n**No external authority retrieved.**
              The research call failed. The conclusions below are generated analysis
              based on the reported transaction facts. No state rule, regulator guidance,
              or approval process was verified in this research run.\n\n## Required
              pre-close work\n\n| Work | Why | Proposed owner | Needed by | Evidence
              to proceed | Fallback |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Build a state
              matrix for all Harbor-licensed states | Notice, approval, surrender,
              and transition rules differ by state | Regulatory counsel with licensing
              team | Before final migration design | Written state-by-state conclusion,
              filing type, deadline, and regulator response | Keep Harbor customers
              outside Mosaic until authority is confirmed |\n| Prioritize the four
              states where only Harbor is licensed | Mosaic appears to lack independent
              authority there | Regulatory counsel | Before any launch commitment
              | Mosaic license, written approval, or another confirmed legal basis
              | Do not offer regulated services in those states |\n| Confirm which
              entity will be the legal service provider after close | The licensed
              entity must match the entity conducting the regulated activity | Deal
              counsel and product counsel | Before customer notices and contract assignment
              | Funds-flow diagram, customer contract, account terms, and operating
              model | Keep Harbor as provider during a regulator-approved transition
              |\n| Identify required notices and approvals | An asset sale may trigger
              asset-transfer, business-change, control, name, location, key-person,
              or surrender filings | Licensing team | Before each state deadline |
              Filing receipts and any required approvals or non-objections | Delay
              the affected state migration |\n| Obtain an interim-operation answer
              for each affected state | A pending filing does not necessarily permit
              operation | Regulatory counsel | Before close | Written authority, regulator
              confirmation, or a clearly applicable rule | Disable transactions or
              restrict access in that state |\n| Plan Harbor’s license surrender or
              run-off | Early surrender could remove the authority needed for open
              transactions, claims, examinations, or refunds | Harbor compliance and
              deal counsel | As part of closing conditions | Regulator-approved surrender
              or run-off plan | Keep the license, bonds, and responsible staff in
              place |\n| Protect required financial assurances | Bonds, permissible
              investments, net worth, and reporting duties may continue during transition
              | Finance and licensing team | Before funds or obligations move | Updated
              bonds, financial statements, and regulator filings | Hold affected balances
              and obligations in the existing licensed structure |\n\n## Notice and
              approval analysis\n\nThe team should not limit its review to provisions
              called “license transfer.” The relevant rule may instead appear under:\n\n-
              transfer of substantially all assets;\n- change in control or ownership;\n-
              merger or corporate reorganization;\n- change in legal entity or licensed
              name;\n- change in business plan;\n- change in responsible individuals;\n-
              change in locations or agents;\n- assignment of customer obligations;\n-
              surrender, suspension, or termination of a license; or\n- acquisition
              of outstanding payment obligations.\n\nA pure asset sale may not meet
              a state’s technical definition of “change of control.” That does **not**
              mean no filing is required. The seller’s disposition of the business
              and the buyer’s start of regulated activity can create separate requirements.\n\nSome
              filings may be notices after signing or before closing. Others may require
              approval before the transaction, before the buyer begins business, or
              before the seller surrenders its license. The applicable timing must
              be verified state by state.\n\n## Interim operation\n\nMosaic should
              not assume it can operate while a new-license or approval request is
              pending. A filed application usually should not be treated as operating
              authority without a verified rule or written regulator position.\n\nA
              possible transition is for Harbor to remain the licensed provider for
              a limited period. This works only if it is legally and operationally
              real:\n\n- Harbor remains responsible to customers.\n- Harbor retains
              control required of the licensee.\n- Customer terms identify the correct
              provider.\n- Customer funds and outstanding obligations remain properly
              covered.\n- Required bonds, permissible investments, reports, records,
              and examinations continue.\n- Mosaic’s role is permitted under applicable
              law.\n- The arrangement does not amount to Mosaic using Harbor’s license
              as a rented license.\n- The transaction documents keep Harbor able to
              perform these duties.\n- Relevant regulators approve or accept the structure
              when required.\n\nThe present plan does not appear to support that model.
              It moves users into Mosaic’s app with one Mosaic account, one balance,
              and access to Mosaic’s products on day one. Those facts point toward
              Mosaic becoming the operating provider. If so, Harbor’s continuing license
              may not solve Mosaic’s authorization gap.\n\n## Transition requirements\n\nThe
              licensing plan should cover more than the four new states. It should
              address:\n\n1. **Outstanding obligations:** Identify which entity owes
              stored balances, transfers, refunds, and claims at each transition point.\n2.
              **Customer contracts:** Confirm whether agreements can be assigned and
              whether notice or consent is required.\n3. **Funds and safeguarding:**
              Map the movement of customer funds and the related permissible-investment
              coverage.\n4. **Surety bonds:** Keep required bonds active until each
              regulator permits release.\n5. **Reports and examinations:** Assign
              responsibility for pre-close and post-close reports, complaints, examinations,
              and record production.\n6. **Books and records:** Preserve Harbor’s
              required records and regulator access after the vendor and corporate
              transition.\n7. **Agents and delegates:** Determine whether any registered
              agents, authorized delegates, or locations need termination or new appointments.\n8.
              **Surrender:** Do not surrender Harbor’s licenses until outstanding
              obligations and regulator conditions are satisfied.\n9. **Customer communications:**
              Ensure notices state the correct provider, effective date, rights, fees,
              and complaint contact.\n10. **Product scope:** Confirm that Mosaic’s
              existing licenses cover all products that migrated users will receive,
              not only Harbor’s former service.\n\n## Recommended closing position\n\nTreat
              authorization for each affected state as a **launch condition**, not
              as a post-close clean-up item.\n\nFor each state, require one of these
              outcomes before Mosaic serves migrated customers:\n\n1. Mosaic already
              has a license that covers the planned activity and product set.\n2.
              Mosaic obtains the required license or approval.\n3. The regulator confirms
              a lawful interim structure.\n4. The affected customers remain with Harbor
              under a supportable run-off model.\n5. Regulated functionality is blocked
              until authority exists.\n\nThe four Harbor-only states should not be
              presented as part of Mosaic’s available footprint until one of these
              paths is documented. If the state review cannot finish before close,
              the most defensible fallback is a state-based migration hold. Mosaic
              can close the asset acquisition without activating regulated service
              in those states.\n\nThis result does not materially change the saved
              working position. It gives that position a clearer operational rule:
              **no regulator-confirmed authority, no day-one regulated operation by
              Mosaic in the affected state.**", "actor": "counsel-copilot", "origin":

              what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations?
            consequence: Whether the missing underlying documents create a compliance
              gap depends on how Mosaic plans to satisfy its own CIP/recordkeeping
              obligations for these users.
            state: answered
            answer: It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program permits
              reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must confirm.
            answer_kind: reported_fact
            linked_fact_ids: *id024
          - question_id: Q-MTL
            text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
              what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
              before onboarding those customers?
            consequence: Whether the four new markets can be served at close depends
              on license transferability and state approval, which is a gating regulatory
              question.
            state: answered
            answer: Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor's licenses
              for the four new markets.
            answer_kind: reported_fact

            text: How is the $50 welcome bonus structured?
            consequence: The structure determines whether the bonus triggers consumer
              disclosure, funds-flow, or state promotional requirements.
            state: left_open
            answer: null
            answer_kind: null
            linked_fact_ids: *id026

            text: Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10

              Mosaic Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and

              has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents

    regulator confirms a lawful path.\n\nAn asset purchase usually leaves the license
    with the licensed seller. It does not automatically move the license to the buyer.
    The buyer generally needs its own authority before it conducts regulated money
    transmission. A contract that says Mosaic “assumes” the licenses does not bind
    a regulator.\n\nThis makes the proposed four-state expansion a closing issue.
    It may also affect Harbor customers in states where both companies already hold
    licenses because the operating entity, customer agreement, custody of funds, or
    licensed activity can change.\n\n**No external authority retrieved.** The research
    call failed. The conclusions below are generated analysis based on the reported
    transaction facts. No state rule, regulator guidance, or approval process was
    verified in this research run.\n\n## Required pre-close work\n\n| Work | Why |

    key-person, or surrender filings | Licensing team | Before each state deadline

    | A pending filing does not necessarily permit operation | Regulatory counsel
    | Before close | Written authority, regulator confirmation, or a clearly applicable
    rule | Disable transactions or restrict access in that state |\n| Plan Harbor’s
    license surrender or run-off | Early surrender could remove the authority needed
    for open transactions, claims, examinations, or refunds | Harbor compliance and
    deal counsel | As part of closing conditions | Regulator-approved surrender or
    run-off plan | Keep the license, bonds, and responsible staff in place |\n| Protect
    required financial assurances | Bonds, permissible investments, net worth, and
    reporting duties may continue during transition | Finance and licensing team |
    Before funds or obligations move | Updated bonds, financial statements, and regulator
    filings | Hold affected balances and obligations in the existing licensed structure
    |\n\n## Notice and approval analysis\n\nThe team should not limit its review to
    provisions called “license transfer.” The relevant rule may instead appear under:\n\n-
    transfer of substantially all assets;\n- change in control or ownership;\n- merger
    or corporate reorganization;\n- change in legal entity or licensed name;\n- change
    in business plan;\n- change in responsible individuals;\n- change in locations
    or agents;\n- assignment of customer obligations;\n- surrender, suspension, or
    termination of a license; or\n- acquisition of outstanding payment obligations.\n\nA
    pure asset sale may not meet a state’s technical definition of “change of control.”
    That does **not** mean no filing is required. The seller’s disposition of the
    business and the buyer’s start of regulated activity can create separate requirements.\n\nSome
    filings may be notices after signing or before closing. Others may require approval
    before the transaction, before the buyer begins business, or before the seller
    surrenders its license. The applicable timing must be verified state by state.\n\n##
    Interim operation\n\nMosaic should not assume it can operate while a new-license
    or approval request is pending. A filed application usually should not be treated
    as operating authority without a verified rule or written regulator position.\n\nA
    possible transition is for Harbor to remain the licensed provider for a limited
    period. This works only if it is legally and operationally real:\n\n- Harbor remains
    responsible to customers.\n- Harbor retains control required of the licensee.\n-
    Customer terms identify the correct provider.\n- Customer funds and outstanding
    obligations remain properly covered.\n- Required bonds, permissible investments,
    reports, records, and examinations continue.\n- Mosaic’s role is permitted under
    applicable law.\n- The arrangement does not amount to Mosaic using Harbor’s license
    as a rented license.\n- The transaction documents keep Harbor able to perform
    these duties.\n- Relevant regulators approve or accept the structure when required.\n\nThe
    present plan does not appear to support that model. It moves users into Mosaic’s
    app with one Mosaic account, one balance, and access to Mosaic’s products on day
    one. Those facts point toward Mosaic becoming the operating provider. If so, Harbor’s
    continuing license may not solve Mosaic’s authorization gap.\n\n## Transition
    requirements\n\nThe licensing plan should cover more than the four new states.
    It should address:\n\n1. **Outstanding obligations:** Identify which entity owes

    **Reports and examinations:** Assign responsibility for pre-close and post-close

    closing position\n\nTreat authorization for each affected state as a **launch

      path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8
    request_text: '# Original Request


      From: Dana, PM — Growth & Integration

      Subject: Harbor migration — anything here need legal?


      We''re acquiring Harbor Pay. Close is targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks). Migration
      plan:


      240k consumer users, 12k business accounts move into our app on day 1 post-close.
      One unified account, one balance, full access to our product set.

      No re-verification — they were already KYC''d by Harbor.

      Harbor holds MTLs in 38 states, we hold 41. Combined that''s 44 — nice win,
      opens four new markets.

      Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024. We have pass/fail
      results for everyone, but not the underlying documents for users onboarded before
      2023.

      Harbor''s monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close.
      Plan is to repoint their transaction feed at our engine on day 1.

      Marketing wants a "Welcome" campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer, launching
      close+1.

      Diligence flagged that Harbor has ~40 open alerts and "a handful" of SARs from
      the last year. Nobody''s read them yet.


      Does any of this need legal before close? It''s really just a data migration.

      '
    recommendation:
      matter_id: MAT-20260909-d89ad8
      path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/recommendations.md
      content: '## Working position


        The Harbor Pay migration needs legal and compliance review before the planned
        close. The leading concern is that an asset purchase generally requires Mosaic
        Relay to confirm its own authority to operate in each state; the current plan
        to use or assume Harbor''s licenses is not established as legally effective.


        The second concern is BSA/AML readiness. Mosaic Relay has not confirmed whether
        its AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC, and underlying
        records are missing for some pre-2023 users. Harbor''s open alerts and SAR
        history also remain unread. These gaps make a day-one migration without re-verification
        or account restrictions difficult to support.


        Transaction monitoring continuity is also material because Harbor''s vendor
        ends at close. The repointed feed should be tested and validated before migrated
        users receive full access. The $50 bonus is lower priority but still needs
        review once its eligibility, funding, terms, and disclosures are known.


        ## Plausible alternatives


        A narrower launch could exclude the four new markets, restrict users whose
        KYC evidence is incomplete, or delay full product access until alert review
        and monitoring validation finish. A full day-one launch remains possible only
        if state licensing, AML/CIP reliance, alert handling, and monitoring continuity
        are confirmed.


        ## Material facts and assumptions


        Reported facts include the asset-purchase structure, the current plan to rely
        on Harbor''s licenses, the lack of a compliance answer on KYC reliance, and
        the unread alerts and SAR history. The analysis assumes both entities conduct
        regulated money-transmission activity and that Mosaic Relay will become the
        operating provider immediately after close. It does not assume that Harbor''s
        licenses transfer or that Harbor''s KYC is sufficient.


        ## What could change this view


        The view could change if state counsel confirms an effective licensing path
        for each affected state, compliance confirms permissible reliance with adequate
        records or remediation, diligence clears the alerts and SAR history, and testing
        shows no monitoring gap. The bonus structure remains unknown.


        ## Support limit


        This is generated analysis based on reported matter facts. No external authority
        was retrieved.'

        number: 2
        content: '**No external authority retrieved**


          ## Practical answer


          **Do not treat Harbor’s 38 money transmitter licenses as transferable assets.**
          For closing purposes, assume that Mosaic cannot use them unless each relevant
          state regulator confirms a lawful path.


          An asset purchase usually leaves the license with the licensed seller. It
          does not automatically move the license to the buyer. The buyer generally
          needs its own authority before it conducts regulated money transmission.
          A contract that says Mosaic “assumes” the licenses does not bind a regulator.


          This makes the proposed four-state expansion a closing issue. It may also
          affect Harbor customers in states where both companies already hold licenses
          because the operating entity, customer agreement, custody of funds, or licensed
          activity can change.


          **No external authority retrieved.** The research call failed. The conclusions
          below are generated analysis based on the reported transaction facts. No
          state rule, regulator guidance, or approval process was verified in this
          research run.


          ## Required pre-close work


          | Work | Why | Proposed owner | Needed by | Evidence to proceed | Fallback
          |

          |---|---|---|---|---|---|

          | Build a state matrix for all Harbor-licensed states | Notice, approval,
          surrender, and transition rules differ by state | Regulatory counsel with
          licensing team | Before final migration design | Written state-by-state
          conclusion, filing type, deadline, and regulator response | Keep Harbor
          customers outside Mosaic until authority is confirmed |

          | Prioritize the four states where only Harbor is licensed | Mosaic appears
          to lack independent authority there | Regulatory counsel | Before any launch
          commitment | Mosaic license, written approval, or another confirmed legal
          basis | Do not offer regulated services in those states |

          | Confirm which entity will be the legal service provider after close |
          The licensed entity must match the entity conducting the regulated activity
          | Deal counsel and product counsel | Before customer notices and contract
          assignment | Funds-flow diagram, customer contract, account terms, and operating
          model | Keep Harbor as provider during a regulator-approved transition |

          | Identify required notices and approvals | An asset sale may trigger asset-transfer,
          business-change, control, name, location, key-person, or surrender filings
          | Licensing team | Before each state deadline | Filing receipts and any
          required approvals or non-objections | Delay the affected state migration
          |

          | Obtain an interim-operation answer for each affected state | A pending
          filing does not necessarily permit operation | Regulatory counsel | Before
          close | Written authority, regulator confirmation, or a clearly applicable
          rule | Disable transactions or restrict access in that state |

          | Plan Harbor’s license surrender or run-off | Early surrender could remove
          the authority needed for open transactions, claims, examinations, or refunds
          | Harbor compliance and deal counsel | As part of closing conditions | Regulator-approved
          surrender or run-off plan | Keep the license, bonds, and responsible staff
          in place |

          | Protect required financial assurances | Bonds, permissible investments,
          net worth, and reporting duties may continue during transition | Finance
          and licensing team | Before funds or obligations move | Updated bonds, financial
          statements, and regulator filings | Hold affected balances and obligations
          in the existing licensed structure |


          ## Notice and approval analysis


          The team should not limit its review to provisions called “license transfer.”
          The relevant rule may instead appear under:


          - transfer of substantially all assets;

          - change in control or ownership;

          - merger or corporate reorganization;

          - change in legal entity or licensed name;

          - change in business plan;

          - change in responsible individuals;

          - change in locations or agents;

          - assignment of customer obligations;

          - surrender, suspension, or termination of a license; or

          - acquisition of outstanding payment obligations.


          A pure asset sale may not meet a state’s technical definition of “change
          of control.” That does **not** mean no filing is required. The seller’s
          disposition of the business and the buyer’s start of regulated activity
          can create separate requirements.


          Some filings may be notices after signing or before closing. Others may
          require approval before the transaction, before the buyer begins business,
          or before the seller surrenders its license. The applicable timing must
          be verified state by state.


          ## Interim operation


          Mosaic should not assume it can operate while a new-license or approval
          request is pending. A filed application usually should not be treated as
          operating authority without a verified rule or written regulator position.


          A possible transition is for Harbor to remain the licensed provider for
          a limited period. This works only if it is legally and operationally real:


          - Harbor remains responsible to customers.

          - Harbor retains control required of the licensee.

          - Customer terms identify the correct provider.

          - Customer funds and outstanding obligations remain properly covered.

          - Required bonds, permissible investments, reports, records, and examinations
          continue.

          - Mosaic’s role is permitted under applicable law.

          - The arrangement does not amount to Mosaic using Harbor’s license as a
          rented license.

          - The transaction documents keep Harbor able to perform these duties.

          - Relevant regulators approve or accept the structure when required.


          The present plan does not appear to support that model. It moves users into
          Mosaic’s app with one Mosaic account, one balance, and access to Mosaic’s
          products on day one. Those facts point toward Mosaic becoming the operating
          provider. If so, Harbor’s continuing license may not solve Mosaic’s authorization
          gap.


          ## Transition requirements


          The licensing plan should cover more than the four new states. It should
          address:


          1. **Outstanding obligations:** Identify which entity owes stored balances,
          transfers, refunds, and claims at each transition point.

          2. **Customer contracts:** Confirm whether agreements can be assigned and
          whether notice or consent is required.

          3. **Funds and safeguarding:** Map the movement of customer funds and the
          related permissible-investment coverage.

          4. **Surety bonds:** Keep required bonds active until each regulator permits
          release.

          5. **Reports and examinations:** Assign responsibility for pre-close and
          post-close reports, complaints, examinations, and record production.

          6. **Books and records:** Preserve Harbor’s required records and regulator
          access after the vendor and corporate transition.

          7. **Agents and delegates:** Determine whether any registered agents, authorized
          delegates, or locations need termination or new appointments.

          8. **Surrender:** Do not surrender Harbor’s licenses until outstanding obligations
          and regulator conditions are satisfied.

          9. **Customer communications:** Ensure notices state the correct provider,
          effective date, rights, fees, and complaint contact.

          10. **Product scope:** Confirm that Mosaic’s existing licenses cover all
          products that migrated users will receive, not only Harbor’s former service.


          ## Recommended closing position


          Treat authorization for each affected state as a **launch condition**, not
          as a post-close clean-up item.


          For each state, require one of these outcomes before Mosaic serves migrated
          customers:


          1. Mosaic already has a license that covers the planned activity and product
          set.

          2. Mosaic obtains the required license or approval.

          3. The regulator confirms a lawful interim structure.

          4. The affected customers remain with Harbor under a supportable run-off
          model.

          5. Regulated functionality is blocked until authority exists.


          The four Harbor-only states should not be presented as part of Mosaic’s
          available footprint until one of these paths is documented. If the state
          review cannot finish before close, the most defensible fallback is a state-based
          migration hold. Mosaic can close the asset acquisition without activating
          regulated service in those states.


          This result does not materially change the saved working position. It gives
          that position a clearer operational rule: **no regulator-confirmed authority,
          no day-one regulated operation by Mosaic in the affected state.**'

      facts:
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-182bcc
        text: Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
          out).
        source_ids:
        - REQ-20260909-283892
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-551367
        text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
          Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and
          full access to Mosaic's product set.
        source_ids:
        - REQ-20260909-283892
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9a0c61
        text: Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC'd by Harbor.
        source_ids:
        - REQ-20260909-283892
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-33293c
        text: Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
          Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.
        source_ids:
        - REQ-20260909-283892
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-aea8ec
        text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has
          pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users
          onboarded before 2023.
        source_ids:
        - REQ-20260909-283892
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-073838
        text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
          terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor's transaction feed at Mosaic's
          engine on day 1.
        source_ids:
        - REQ-20260909-283892
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-19aebc
        text: Marketing wants a 'Welcome' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
          launching close+1.
        source_ids:
        - REQ-20260909-283892
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-adf2cb
        text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from the last
          year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.
        source_ids:
        - REQ-20260909-283892
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-4c1fd8
        text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
          Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-9835ba
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f2c49f
        text: Plan is no re-verification of Harbor's existing KYC; Harbor users were
          already KYC'd.
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-9835ba
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-13d4c1
        text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
          results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users
          onboarded before 2023.
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-9835ba
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-78d5cd
        text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
          terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay's
          engine on day 1.
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-9835ba
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9f7bde
        text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from the last
          year at Harbor; none have been read yet.
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-9835ba
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-ed9f06
        text: How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
          buys Harbor's assets)
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-2e549e
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-b5e71e
        text: Does Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another
          institution's prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification required?
          — Not sure / need to check with compliance
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-2e549e
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-849b00
        text: What is known about Harbor's ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last
          year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-2e549e
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f0fb01
        text: For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic
          Relay plan to operate under Harbor's existing licenses or apply for its
          own? — Use/assume Harbor's licenses
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-2e549e
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-620c62
        text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what
          is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
          and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay's
          AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must
          confirm.
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-2e549e
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-070aec
        text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
          been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
          have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-2e549e
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-771ee1
        text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
          is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before onboarding
          those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor's
          licenses for the four new markets.
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-2e549e
      assumptions:
      - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-29b823
        text: Mosaic Relay's existing money transmission licenses and Harbor's MTLs
          are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition without new
          state approval
        reason: Needed to continue
      - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-3c5756
        text: The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own
          BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents
        reason: Needed to continue
      - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-1a519f
        text: The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and validated before
          close without a monitoring gap
        reason: Needed to continue
      - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-ca7dfd
        text: Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state MTL regimes
          and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).
        reason: Needed to continue
      - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-d40239
        text: Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per
          the request).
        reason: Needed to continue
      - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-57e86b
        text: The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase, which affects
          whether Harbor's licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure
          not yet confirmed).
        reason: Needed to continue
      questions:
      - question_id: Q-SAR
        text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
          been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
        consequence: Unread open alerts and SARs are the highest-risk item; they can
          create BSA/AML exposure that must be addressed before close and could affect
          the deal itself.
        state: answered
        answer: The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain
          in diligence.
        answer_kind: reported_fact
        linked_fact_ids:
        - FACT-20260909-070aec
      - question_id: Q-KYC
        text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what
          is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
          and recordkeeping obligations?
        consequence: Whether the missing underlying documents create a compliance
          gap depends on how Mosaic plans to satisfy its own CIP/recordkeeping obligations
          for these users.
        state: answered
        answer: It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program permits
          reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must confirm.
        answer_kind: reported_fact
        linked_fact_ids:
        - FACT-20260909-620c62
      - question_id: Q-MTL
        text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
          is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before onboarding
          those customers?
        consequence: Whether the four new markets can be served at close depends on
          license transferability and state approval, which is a gating regulatory
          question.
        state: answered
        answer: Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor's licenses for
          the four new markets.
        answer_kind: reported_fact
        linked_fact_ids:
        - FACT-20260909-771ee1
      - question_id: Q-BONUS
        text: How is the $50 welcome bonus structured?
        consequence: The structure determines whether the bonus triggers consumer
          disclosure, funds-flow, or state promotional requirements.
        state: left_open
        answer: null
        answer_kind: null
        linked_fact_ids: []

      "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/recommendations.md", "content": "## Working
      position\n\nThe Harbor Pay migration needs legal and compliance review before
      the planned close. The leading concern is that an asset purchase generally requires
      Mosaic Relay to confirm its own authority to operate in each state; the current
      plan to use or assume Harbor''s licenses is not established as legally effective.\n\nThe
      second concern is BSA/AML readiness. Mosaic Relay has not confirmed whether
      its AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC, and underlying
      records are missing for some pre-2023 users. Harbor''s open alerts and SAR history
      also remain unread. These gaps make a day-one migration without re-verification
      or account restrictions difficult to support.\n\nTransaction monitoring continuity
      is also material because Harbor''s vendor ends at close. The repointed feed
      should be tested and validated before migrated users receive full access. The
      $50 bonus is lower priority but still needs review once its eligibility, funding,
      terms, and disclosures are known.\n\n## Plausible alternatives\n\nA narrower
      launch could exclude the four new markets, restrict users whose KYC evidence
      is incomplete, or delay full product access until alert review and monitoring
      validation finish. A full day-one launch remains possible only if state licensing,
      AML/CIP reliance, alert handling, and monitoring continuity are confirmed.\n\n##
      Material facts and assumptions\n\nReported facts include the asset-purchase
      structure, the current plan to rely on Harbor''s licenses, the lack of a compliance
      answer on KYC reliance, and the unread alerts and SAR history. The analysis
      assumes both entities conduct regulated money-transmission activity and that
      Mosaic Relay will become the operating provider immediately after close. It
      does not assume that Harbor''s licenses transfer or that Harbor''s KYC is sufficient.\n\n##
      What could change this view\n\nThe view could change if state counsel confirms
      an effective licensing path for each affected state, compliance confirms permissible
      reliance with adequate records or remediation, diligence clears the alerts and
      SAR history, and testing shows no monitoring gap. The bonus structure remains
      unknown.\n\n## Support limit\n\nThis is generated analysis based on reported
      matter facts. No external authority was retrieved.", "current_version_id": "REC-20260909-7112e7",

      "number": 1, "content": "## Working position\n\nThe Harbor Pay migration needs
      legal and compliance review before the planned close. The leading concern is

      users. Harbor''s open alerts and SAR history also remain unread. These gaps

      include the asset-purchase structure, the current plan to rely on Harbor''s

      "proposal": {"version_id": "REC-20260911-b03b7c", "number": 2, "content": "**No
      external authority retrieved**\n\n## Practical answer\n\n**Do not treat Harbor’s
      38 money transmitter licenses as transferable assets.** For closing purposes,
      assume that Mosaic cannot use them unless each relevant state regulator confirms
      a lawful path.\n\nAn asset purchase usually leaves the license with the licensed
      seller. It does not automatically move the license to the buyer. The buyer generally
      needs its own authority before it conducts regulated money transmission. A contract
      that says Mosaic “assumes” the licenses does not bind a regulator.\n\nThis makes
      the proposed four-state expansion a closing issue. It may also affect Harbor
      customers in states where both companies already hold licenses because the operating
      entity, customer agreement, custody of funds, or licensed activity can change.\n\n**No
      external authority retrieved.** The research call failed. The conclusions below
      are generated analysis based on the reported transaction facts. No state rule,
      regulator guidance, or approval process was verified in this research run.\n\n##
      Required pre-close work\n\n| Work | Why | Proposed owner | Needed by | Evidence
      to proceed | Fallback |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Build a state matrix for
      all Harbor-licensed states | Notice, approval, surrender, and transition rules
      differ by state | Regulatory counsel with licensing team | Before final migration
      design | Written state-by-state conclusion, filing type, deadline, and regulator
      response | Keep Harbor customers outside Mosaic until authority is confirmed
      |\n| Prioritize the four states where only Harbor is licensed | Mosaic appears
      to lack independent authority there | Regulatory counsel | Before any launch
      commitment | Mosaic license, written approval, or another confirmed legal basis
      | Do not offer regulated services in those states |\n| Confirm which entity
      will be the legal service provider after close | The licensed entity must match
      the entity conducting the regulated activity | Deal counsel and product counsel
      | Before customer notices and contract assignment | Funds-flow diagram, customer
      contract, account terms, and operating model | Keep Harbor as provider during
      a regulator-approved transition |\n| Identify required notices and approvals
      | An asset sale may trigger asset-transfer, business-change, control, name,
      location, key-person, or surrender filings | Licensing team | Before each state
      deadline | Filing receipts and any required approvals or non-objections | Delay
      the affected state migration |\n| Obtain an interim-operation answer for each
      affected state | A pending filing does not necessarily permit operation | Regulatory
      counsel | Before close | Written authority, regulator confirmation, or a clearly
      applicable rule | Disable transactions or restrict access in that state |\n|
      Plan Harbor’s license surrender or run-off | Early surrender could remove the
      authority needed for open transactions, claims, examinations, or refunds | Harbor
      compliance and deal counsel | As part of closing conditions | Regulator-approved
      surrender or run-off plan | Keep the license, bonds, and responsible staff in
      place |\n| Protect required financial assurances | Bonds, permissible investments,
      net worth, and reporting duties may continue during transition | Finance and
      licensing team | Before funds or obligations move | Updated bonds, financial
      statements, and regulator filings | Hold affected balances and obligations in
      the existing licensed structure |\n\n## Notice and approval analysis\n\nThe
      team should not limit its review to provisions called “license transfer.” The
      relevant rule may instead appear under:\n\n- transfer of substantially all assets;\n-
      change in control or ownership;\n- merger or corporate reorganization;\n- change
      in legal entity or licensed name;\n- change in business plan;\n- change in responsible
      individuals;\n- change in locations or agents;\n- assignment of customer obligations;\n-
      surrender, suspension, or termination of a license; or\n- acquisition of outstanding
      payment obligations.\n\nA pure asset sale may not meet a state’s technical definition
      of “change of control.” That does **not** mean no filing is required. The seller’s
      disposition of the business and the buyer’s start of regulated activity can
      create separate requirements.\n\nSome filings may be notices after signing or
      before closing. Others may require approval before the transaction, before the
      buyer begins business, or before the seller surrenders its license. The applicable
      timing must be verified state by state.\n\n## Interim operation\n\nMosaic should
      not assume it can operate while a new-license or approval request is pending.
      A filed application usually should not be treated as operating authority without
      a verified rule or written regulator position.\n\nA possible transition is for
      Harbor to remain the licensed provider for a limited period. This works only
      if it is legally and operationally real:\n\n- Harbor remains responsible to
      customers.\n- Harbor retains control required of the licensee.\n- Customer terms
      identify the correct provider.\n- Customer funds and outstanding obligations
      remain properly covered.\n- Required bonds, permissible investments, reports,
      records, and examinations continue.\n- Mosaic’s role is permitted under applicable
      law.\n- The arrangement does not amount to Mosaic using Harbor’s license as
      a rented license.\n- The transaction documents keep Harbor able to perform these
      duties.\n- Relevant regulators approve or accept the structure when required.\n\nThe
      present plan does not appear to support that model. It moves users into Mosaic’s
      app with one Mosaic account, one balance, and access to Mosaic’s products on
      day one. Those facts point toward Mosaic becoming the operating provider. If
      so, Harbor’s continuing license may not solve Mosaic’s authorization gap.\n\n##
      Transition requirements\n\nThe licensing plan should cover more than the four
      new states. It should address:\n\n1. **Outstanding obligations:** Identify which
      entity owes stored balances, transfers, refunds, and claims at each transition
      point.\n2. **Customer contracts:** Confirm whether agreements can be assigned
      and whether notice or consent is required.\n3. **Funds and safeguarding:** Map
      the movement of customer funds and the related permissible-investment coverage.\n4.
      **Surety bonds:** Keep required bonds active until each regulator permits release.\n5.
      **Reports and examinations:** Assign responsibility for pre-close and post-close
      reports, complaints, examinations, and record production.\n6. **Books and records:**
      Preserve Harbor’s required records and regulator access after the vendor and
      corporate transition.\n7. **Agents and delegates:** Determine whether any registered
      agents, authorized delegates, or locations need termination or new appointments.\n8.
      **Surrender:** Do not surrender Harbor’s licenses until outstanding obligations
      and regulator conditions are satisfied.\n9. **Customer communications:** Ensure
      notices state the correct provider, effective date, rights, fees, and complaint
      contact.\n10. **Product scope:** Confirm that Mosaic’s existing licenses cover
      all products that migrated users will receive, not only Harbor’s former service.\n\n##
      Recommended closing position\n\nTreat authorization for each affected state
      as a **launch condition**, not as a post-close clean-up item.\n\nFor each state,
      require one of these outcomes before Mosaic serves migrated customers:\n\n1.
      Mosaic already has a license that covers the planned activity and product set.\n2.
      Mosaic obtains the required license or approval.\n3. The regulator confirms
      a lawful interim structure.\n4. The affected customers remain with Harbor under
      a supportable run-off model.\n5. Regulated functionality is blocked until authority
      exists.\n\nThe four Harbor-only states should not be presented as part of Mosaic’s
      available footprint until one of these paths is documented. If the state review
      cannot finish before close, the most defensible fallback is a state-based migration
      hold. Mosaic can close the asset acquisition without activating regulated service
      in those states.\n\nThis result does not materially change the saved working
      position. It gives that position a clearer operational rule: **no regulator-confirmed
      authority, no day-one regulated operation by Mosaic in the affected state.**",

      questions:
      - question_id: Q-SAR
        text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
          been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
        consequence: Unread open alerts and SARs are the highest-risk item; they can
          create BSA/AML exposure that must be addressed before close and could affect
          the deal itself.
        state: answered
        answer: The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain
          in diligence.
        answer_kind: reported_fact
        linked_fact_ids:
        - FACT-20260909-070aec
      - question_id: Q-KYC
        text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what
          is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
          and recordkeeping obligations?
        consequence: Whether the missing underlying documents create a compliance
          gap depends on how Mosaic plans to satisfy its own CIP/recordkeeping obligations
          for these users.
        state: answered
        answer: It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program permits
          reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must confirm.
        answer_kind: reported_fact
        linked_fact_ids:
        - FACT-20260909-620c62
      - question_id: Q-MTL
        text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
          is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before onboarding
          those customers?
        consequence: Whether the four new markets can be served at close depends on
          license transferability and state approval, which is a gating regulatory
          question.
        state: answered
        answer: Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor's licenses for
          the four new markets.
        answer_kind: reported_fact
        linked_fact_ids:
        - FACT-20260909-771ee1
      - question_id: Q-BONUS
        text: How is the $50 welcome bonus structured?
        consequence: The structure determines whether the bonus triggers consumer
          disclosure, funds-flow, or state promotional requirements.
        state: left_open
        answer: null
        answer_kind: null
