          | --- |

          | # BILL ANALYSIS |


          |     |

          | --- |

          | S.B. 895 |

          | By: Johnson |

          | Pensions, Investments<br>& Financial Services |

          | Committee Report<br>(Unamended) |


          |     |

          | --- |

          | **BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE**<br>Money transmission is currently<br>regulated
          by statutes that vary widely among the different states, and the industry<br>has
          voiced concerns about the need to comply with so many different<br>requirements.
          Additionally, the current Texas statutes regulating money<br>transmission
          were originally adopted in 2005, but the business of money<br>transmission
          has significantly changed and expanded since that time. S.B. 895<br>seeks
          to update and streamline regulations to better accommodate the<br>increasing
          number of money transmitters operating within Texas and nationwide<br>by
          providing a clear set of standards that can be implemented by Texas<br>agencies
          in a consistent and coordinated manner for domestic and<br>international
          money transmitters. |

          | **CRIMINAL JUSTICE IMPACT**<br>It is the committee''s opinion<br>that
          this bill expressly does one or more of the following: creates a<br>criminal
          offense, increases the punishment for an existing criminal offense<br>or
          category of offenses, or changes the eligibility of a person for community<br>supervision,
          parole, or mandatory supervision. |

          | **RULEMAKING AUTHORITY**<br>It is the committee''s opinion<br>that rulemaking
          authority is expressly granted to the Finance Commission of<br>Texas in
          SECTIONS 1.01 and 4.01 of this bill. |

          | **ANALYSIS**<br>S.B. 895 amends the Finance<br>Code to modernize the regulation
          of money services businesses. The bill<br>repeals the Money Services Act
          and replaces the act with the Money Services<br>Modernization Act to protect
          the interests of money services purchasers and<br>the public, preserve and
          protect the safety and soundness of money services<br>businesses, and protect
          against drug trafficking, terrorist funding, and<br>money laundering, structuring,
          or related financial crimes. The bill includes<br>money transmission services
          and currency exchange services in the definition<br>of money services, and
          provides for the licensing and regulation of both such<br>types of money
          services. The bill expressly does not authorize the creation<br>of any centralized
          bank digital currency or any other action that prohibits<br>or limits the
          use of paper currency. <br>**Administrative and**<br>**Implementation Provisions**<br>S.B.
          895 requires the Texas<br>Department of Banking to administer the bill and
          authorizes the Finance<br>Commission of Texas to adopt rules to administer
          and enforce the bill in<br>substantially the same manner as provided in
          the provisions repealed by the<br>bill. The bill authorizes the banking
          commissioner of Texas, or a person<br>designated by the commissioner and
          acting under the commissioner''s direction<br>and authority, to do the following:<br>·enter
          into agreements or relationships with government<br>officials, federal and
          state regulatory agencies, and regulatory associations<br>to improve efficiencies
          and reduce regulatory burden by standardizing methods<br>or procedures and
          sharing resources, records, or related information obtained<br>under the
          bill;<br>·use, hire, contract for, or employ analytical systems, methods,<br>or
          software to examine or investigate a person subject to the bill;<br>·accept
          licensing, examination, or investigation reports made by<br>other state
          or federal government agencies or officials; and<br>·accept audit reports
          made by an independent certified public<br>accountant or other qualified
          third-party auditor for an applicant or money<br>services licensee and incorporate
          the audit report in a report of examination<br>or investigation.<br>The
          bill additionally provides<br>for the commissioner''s general authority
          under the bill''s provisions and<br>other law. <br>S.B. 895 makes confidential
          and<br>exempts from state public information law the following information:<br>·all
          information or reports obtained by the commissioner from an<br>applicant,
          money services licensee, or authorized delegate;<br>·all information contained
          in or related to an examination,<br>investigation, operating report, or
          condition report prepared by, on behalf<br>of, or for the use of the commissioner;
          and<br>·financial statements, balance sheets, or authorized delegate<br>information.<br>An
          "authorized<br>delegate," for purposes of the bill, is a person designated
          by a money<br>transmission licensee to engage in money transmission services
          on behalf of<br>the licensee. The bill establishes the circumstances under
          which and the<br>persons to whom the commissioner may disclose information
          not otherwise<br>subject to disclosure under the bill and clarifies that
          the bill does not<br>prohibit the commissioner from disclosing to the public
          a list of all money<br>services licensees or the aggregated financial or
          transactional data<br>concerning those licensees. The bill specifies the
          information for each money<br>services licensee contained in the department''s
          records that is not<br>confidential and may be made available to the public
          in its entirety on the<br>department''s website or in the nationwide multistate
          licensing system and registry<br>(NMLS), or in response to a written request
          for the information received by<br>the department.<br>S.B. 895 provides
          for the<br>commissioner''s authority regarding conducting investigations
          in or outside<br>Texas and the United States as the commissioner considers
          necessary or<br>appropriate to administer or enforce the bill in substantially
          the same<br>manner as in provisions repealed by the bill. The bill sets
          out provisions<br>relating to the commissioner''s authority to conduct examinations
          and<br>investigations of a money services licensee or authorized delegate
          or take<br>other action under the bill or a related rule or order as reasonably<br>necessary
          or appropriate to administer and enforce the bill and any other<br>applicable
          law. The bill requires a money services licensee or authorized<br>delegate
          to provide records reasonably requested by the commissioner for<br>examination,
          at the location and in the format specified by the commissioner,<br>and
          to pay all costs reasonably incurred in connection with the examination.<br>The
          bill additionally sets out provisions relating to the commissioner''s<br>participation
          in multistate supervisory processes established between states to<br>share
          certain information regarding money services licensees that hold<br>licenses
          in Texas and other states, including provisions prohibiting the<br>commissioner
          from waiving the commissioner''s authority under the bill with<br>respect
          to examinations, investigations, or other authorized action. A joint<br>examination
          or investigation, or acceptance of an examination or<br>investigation report,
          does not waive an examination assessment provided for<br>in the bill.<br>S.B.
          895 establishes the<br>relationship between its provisions and federal law
          governing money<br>transmission with regard to any inconsistency between
          the bill and that<br>federal law. The bill establishes, in the same manner
          as provisions repealed<br>by the bill, that a money services licensee, an
          authorized delegate, or a<br>person who knowingly engages in activities
          that are regulated and require such<br>a license is considered to have consented
          to the jurisdiction of Texas courts<br>for all actions arising under the
          bill. The bill additionally establishes<br>that a person is presumed to
          exercise a controlling influence over a money<br>services licensee if the
          person holds the power to directly or indirectly<br>vote not less than 10
          percent of the outstanding voting shares or voting<br>interests of a money
          services licensee or person in control of such a<br>licensee. This presumption
          may be rebutted by evidence that the person who is<br>presumed to exercise
          a controlling influence is a passive investor. The bill<br>specifies the
          method for determining the percentage of a money services<br>licensee controlled
          by a person for the bill''s purposes.<br>**Money Services Licenses**<br>S.B.
          895 prohibits a person,<br>defined by the bill as an individual or a corporate
          entity identified by the<br>commissioner, from engaging in the business
          of money transmission or the<br>business of currency exchange or from advertising,
          soliciting, or holding<br>itself out as doing so unless the person is licensed
          under the bill to do so.<br>The bill establishes that a person engages in
          the money transmission business<br>or the currency exchange business if
          the person receives or expects to<br>receive compensation, directly or indirectly,
          for conducting money transmission<br>or exchanging currency, respectively.
          The bill defines the following terms<br>with respect to the scope of a money
          transmission license:<br>·"money transmission" means selling or issuing
          payment<br>instruments or stored value to, or receiving money or monetary
          value for<br>transmission services from, a person physically located in
          Texas for a<br>transaction requested in person and, for a transaction requested<br>electronically
          or by phone, a determination based on certain information that<br>the person
          requesting the transaction is in Texas;<br>·"money" or "monetary value"
          means currency<br>or a claim that can be converted into currency through
          a financial<br>institution, electronic payments network, or other formal
          or informal payment<br>system, including stablecoin that is pegged to a
          sovereign currency, is fully<br>backed by assets held in reserve, and grants
          a holder of the stablecoin the<br>right to redeem the stablecoin for sovereign
          currency from the issuer;<br>·"payment instrument" means a written or electronic<br>check,
          draft, money order, traveler''s check, or other written or electronic<br>instrument
          for the transmission or payment of money or monetary value,<br>whether or
          not the instrument is negotiable, and does not include stored<br>value,
          an instrument redeemable only for certain goods or services, or an<br>instrument
          issued and distributed as part of a loyalty, rewards, or<br>promotional
          program; and<br>·"stored value" means monetary value representing a<br>claim
          against the issuer evidenced by an electronic or digital record and<br>that
          is intended and accepted for use as a means of redemption for money or<br>monetary
          value or payment for goods or services, including prepaid access as<br>defined
          by federal regulations, but does not include a payment instrument,<br>closed-loop
          stored value, or stored value issued and distributed as part of a<br>loyalty,
          rewards, or promotional program.<br>The bill defines the following<br>terms
          with respect to a currency exchange license:<br>·"currency" means the coin
          and paper money issued by a<br>country that is designated as legal tender,
          circulates, and is customarily<br>used and accepted as a medium of exchange
          in the country of issuance; and<br>·"currency exchange" means receiving
          the currency of<br>one government or a negotiable instrument and exchanging
          it for another<br>government''s currency.<br>A money transmission license
          and a currency exchange<br>license are not transferable or assignable. <br>S.B.
          895 establishes that its licensing requirements do<br>not apply to the following:<br>·an
          operator of a payment system to the extent that the<br>operator provides
          processing, clearing, or settlement services, between or<br>among persons
          exempted by this section or money services licensees, in<br>connection with
          wire transfers, credit card transactions, debit card<br>transactions, stored-value
          transactions, automated clearing house transfers,<br>or similar funds transfers;<br>·a
          person appointed as an agent of a payee to collect and<br>process a payment
          from a payor to the payee for goods or services, other than<br>money transmission
          services, provided to the payor by the payee, provided<br>that:<br>othere<br>exists
          a written agreement between the payee and the agent directing the<br>agent
          to collect and process payments from payors on the payee''s behalf;<br>othe<br>payee
          holds the agent out to the public as accepting payments for goods or<br>services
          on the payee''s behalf; and<br>opayment<br>for the goods and services is
          treated as received by the payee on receipt by<br>the agent, the payor''s
          obligation is extinguished, and there is no risk of<br>loss to the payor
          if the agent fails to remit the funds to the payee;<br>·a person who acts
          as an intermediary by processing payments<br>between an entity that has
          directly incurred an outstanding money<br>transmission obligation to a sender,
          and the sender''s designated recipient,<br>provided that the entity that
          has incurred the outstanding money transmission<br>obligation:<br>ois<br>licensed
          or exempt from the licensing requirements of this chapter;<br>oprovides<br>a
          receipt, electronic record, or other written confirmation to the sender<br>identifying
          the entity as the provider of money transmission in the<br>transaction;
          and<br>obears<br>sole responsibility to satisfy the outstanding money transmission
          obligation<br>to the sender, including the obligation to make the sender
          whole in<br>connection with a failure to transmit the funds to the sender''s
          designated<br>recipient;<br>·the United States or a department, agency,
          or instrumentality<br>of the United States, or an agent of a department,
          agency, or instrumentality<br>of the United States;<br>·money transmission
          services by the U.S. Postal Service or by<br>an agent of the service;<br>·a
          state, county, city, or any other governmental agency or<br>governmental
          subdivision or instrumentality of a state, or its agent;<br>·a federally
          insured depository financial institution, bank<br>holding company, office
          of an international banking corporation, foreign bank<br>that establishes
          a federal branch under the federal International Banking Act<br>of 1978,
          a corporation organized under the federal Bank Service Company Act,<br>or
          a corporation organized under the federal Edge Act; <br>·a person expressly
          appointed as a third-party service provider<br>to or agent of an entity
          exempt under the preceding bulleted item, solely to<br>the extent that:<br>othe<br>service
          provider or agent engages in money transmission services on behalf of<br>and
          under a written agreement with the exempt entity that provides the<br>specific
          functions that the service provider or agent is to perform; and<br>othe<br>exempt
          entity assumes all risk of loss and all legal responsibility for<br>satisfying
          the outstanding money transmission obligations owed to purchasers<br>and
          holders of the outstanding money transmission obligations on receipt of<br>the
          purchaser''s or holder''s money or monetary value by the service provider<br>or
          agent;<br>·a trust company, as defined by the Texas Trust Company Act,<br>that
          is organized under state law;<br>·an attorney or title company that in connection
          with a real<br>property transaction receives and disburses domestic currency
          or issues an<br>escrow or trust fund check only on behalf of a party to
          the transaction;<br>·an electronic funds transfer of governmental benefits
          for a<br>federal, state, county, or governmental agency by a contractor
          on behalf of<br>the United States or a department, agency, or instrumentality
          of the United<br>States, or on behalf of a state or governmental subdivision,
          agency, or<br>instrumentality of a state;<br>·a board of trade designated
          as a contract market under the<br>federal Commodity Exchange Act or a person
          who, in the ordinary course of<br>business, provides clearance and settlement
          services for a board of trade to<br>the extent of its operation as or for
          a board of trade;<br>·a registered futures commission merchant under the
          federal<br>commodities laws to the extent of its operation as such a merchant;<br>·a
          person registered as a securities broker-dealer under<br>federal or state
          securities laws to the extent of the person''s operation as a<br>broker-dealer;<br>·an
          individual employed by a money services licensee,<br>authorized delegate,
          or person exempted from the licensing requirements of<br>the bill''s provisions
          when acting within the scope of employment and under<br>the supervision
          of the licensee, authorized delegate, or exempted person as<br>an employee
          and not as an independent contractor; and<br>·a person exempt by a regulation
          or order of the commissioner<br>finding that:<br>othe<br>exemption is in
          the public interest; and<br>othe<br>regulation of the person is not necessary
          for the purposes of the bill''s<br>provisions.<br>The bill authorizes the<br>commissioner
          to require a person claiming to be exempt from licensing to<br>provide information
          and documentation demonstrating that the person qualifies<br>for the exemption
          claimed. On receiving a license application and finding<br>that the exemption
          is in the public interest, the commissioner may exempt the<br>following
          persons from the applicable licensing requirements: <br>·for a money transmission
          license, a person who takes certain<br>action related to the money transmission
          business only for the purpose of<br>engaging in the person''s primary business;
          and<br>·for a currency exchange license, a retailer, wholesaler, or<br>service
          provider that in the ordinary course of business accepts currency of<br>a
          foreign country or government as payment for goods or services, subject
          to<br>certain limitations specified by the bill.<br>The commissioner may
          examine a<br>person to verify the person''s exempt status based on those
          exemption reasons.<br>The bill authorizes a currency exchange licensee to
          engage in the currency<br>exchange business at one or more locations in
          Texas directly or indirectly owned<br>by the licensee under a single license.<br>S.B.
          895 requires an applicant<br>for a money services license to apply in a
          form and medium prescribed by the<br>commissioner and requires such a form
          to contain content as provided by commission<br>rule or the commissioner''s
          instruction or procedure. The commissioner may<br>update the form in accordance
          with applicable law in order to carry out the<br>bill''s purposes and maintain
          consistency with NMLS licensing standards and<br>practices. The bill prescribes
          the information the application must contain<br>and the additional information
          that must be provided by an applicant that is<br>a corporation, limited
          liability company, partnership, or other legal entity.<br>The bill authorizes
          the commissioner to waive one or more such application<br>requirements or
          permit an applicant to submit other information in lieu of<br>the prescribed
          information and requires a license applicant to file with the<br>department
          at the time of application a nonrefundable application fee in the<br>amount
          established by commission rule. <br>S.B. 895 sets out additional<br>information
          requirements applicable to an individual who is in control of a<br>money
          services licensee or applicant, who seeks to acquire control of a money<br>services
          licensee, or who is a key individual, defined by the bill as an<br>individual
          who is ultimately responsible for establishing or directing the<br>policies
          and procedures of a money services licensee, including an executive<br>officer,
          manager, director, or trustee. This additional information must<br>include
          the following with respect to an individual subject to the<br>requirements:<br>·fingerprints
          for submission to the FBI and the commissioner for<br>purposes of a national
          criminal history background check unless the person<br>currently resides
          outside of the United States and has resided outside of the<br>United States
          for the 10-year period preceding the submission of the application;<br>and<br>·personal
          history and experience, in a form and medium<br>prescribed by the commissioner,
          that contains an independent credit report<br>for an individual with a social
          security number, information related to any<br>criminal convictions or pending
          charges against the individual, and<br>information related to any regulatory
          or administrative action and any civil<br>litigation against the individual
          involving claims of fraud,<br>misrepresentation, conversion, mismanagement
          of funds, breach of fiduciary<br>duty, or breach of contract.<br>An individual
          who is subject to<br>these additional information requirements and who has
          resided outside of the<br>United States at any time in the preceding 10
          years must also provide an<br>investigative background report prepared by
          an independent search firm that<br>meets the bill''s minimum specified requirements.<br>S.B.
          895, with regard to the<br>issuance of a money services license:<br>·establishes
          that an application appearing to include all<br>required items and address
          all required matters is considered complete and<br>clarifies that the commissioner''s
          determination of completeness and<br>acceptance for processing is not an
          assessment of the application''s<br>substance;<br>·requires the commissioner
          to promptly notify the applicant in<br>writing of the date on which the
          application is determined complete and to<br>approve or deny the application
          not later than the 120th day after that date;<br>·if the commissioner does
          not approve or deny the application<br>within that period, provides for
          the application approval and effective<br>license date and authorizes the
          commissioner to extend the application<br>approval period for good cause;<br>·requires
          the commissioner to investigate the applicant''s<br>financial condition
          and responsibility, financial and business experience,<br>character, and
          general fitness;<br>·authorizes the commissioner to conduct an on-site investigation<br>of
          the applicant with reasonable costs payable by the applicant; <br>·requires
          the commissioner to issue a license to an applicant if<br>the commissioner
          finds the applicant has complied with the applicable<br>application and
          information requirements and that it is in the interest of<br>the public
          to permit the applicant to engage in money transmission, currency<br>exchange,
          or both, considering certain financial, business, and personal<br>qualities,
          as applicable, of the applicant or a key individual or person in<br>control
          of the applicant;<br>·for an applicant who participates in or is otherwise
          subject to<br>a multistate licensing process, provides for the commissioner''s
          authority to<br>investigate the applicant or accept the investigation results
          of another<br>state; and <br>·establishes the license term takes effect
          on the day the<br>application is approved. <br>The bill requires an applicant<br>for
          a money transmission license or a currency exchange license to<br>demonstrate
          that it meets or will meet all bill requirements relating to<br>securities,
          investments, and other financial requirements, as applicable, and<br>requires
          a licensee to continue to meet those requirements at all times. <br>S.B.
          895 sets out provisions<br>relating to the following with regard to money
          services licenses that are<br>substantially the same as provisions repealed
          by the bill: <br>·the use of the NMLS for obtaining certain applicant information<br>or
          fee payments;<br>·the commissioner''s duty to provide notice of a license
          denial<br>for an applicant who does not meet the requisite qualifications
          or satisfy<br>the requirements for the license and the process for requesting
          a hearing to<br>appeal the denial;<br>·the commissioner''s authority to
          suspend or revoke the license<br>of a license holder who does not continue
          to meet the qualifications or<br>satisfy the provisions relating to the
          license holder''s duty to annually pay<br>a license fee and submit a report
          containing certain financial information;<br>·surrendering a license and
          filing a new license application for<br>an expired or surrendered license;
          and<br>·the nonrefundable nature of a fee or cost paid by a licensee<br>under
          the bill.<br>**Acquisition of Control and**<br>**Change of Key Individual**<br>S.B.
          895 requires a person or<br>group of persons acting in concert seeking to
          acquire control of a money<br>services licensee to obtain the written approval
          from the commissioner before<br>acquiring control. The bill defines "control"
          as the power to<br>directly or indirectly vote at least 25 percent of the
          outstanding voting<br>shares or voting interests of a money services licensee
          or person in control<br>of a licensee, the power to elect or appoint a majority
          of key individuals or<br>other persons exercising managerial authority of
          a person in control of a<br>licensee, or the power to directly or indirectly
          exercise a controlling<br>influence over the management or policies of a
          licensee or person in control<br>of a money services license. The bill provides
          the following with respect to<br>an application to acquire control of a
          money services licensee:<br>·requires the person or group, in cooperation
          with the licensee,<br>to submit an application in a form and medium prescribed
          by the commissioner<br>and to submit a nonrefundable fee in the amount established
          by commission<br>rule;<br>·authorizes the commissioner, on request, to permit
          the<br>licensee, person, or group to submit some or all of the required
          information<br>without using the NMLS;<br>·requires the application to include,
          from the bill''s<br>information requirements for certain individuals, information
          for any new key<br>individual that has not previously completed those requirements;<br>·establishes
          that an application is considered complete when it<br>appears to include
          all required items and address all required matters and further<br>clarifies
          that the commissioner''s determination of completeness and<br>acceptance
          for processing is not an assessment of the application''s<br>substance;<br>·requires
          the commissioner to promptly notify the applicant in<br>writing of the date
          on which the application is determined complete and to<br>approve or deny
          the application not later than the 60th day after that date;<br>·if the
          application is not approved or denied before the 61st<br>day after the completion
          date, provides for the application''s approval and acquisition<br>of control
          and authorizes the commissioner to extend the application period<br>for
          good cause;<br>·requires the commissioner to investigate the financial<br>condition
          and responsibility, financial and business experience, character,<br>and
          general fitness of the person or group seeking to acquire control;<br>·requires
          the commissioner to approve the acquisition of control<br>if the commissioner
          finds that the applicable application, fee, and<br>information requirements
          have been met and that it is in the interest of the<br>public to permit
          the person or group to control the money services licensee<br>considering
          certain financial, business, and personal qualities, as<br>applicable, of
          the person or group seeking to acquire control or of the key<br>individuals
          and persons that would be in control of the licensee after the<br>acquisition
          of control;<br>·for an applicant who participates in or is otherwise subject
          to<br>a multistate licensing process, provides for the commissioner''s authority
          to<br>investigate an applicant or accept the investigation results of another<br>state;
          and<br>·requires the commissioner to inform the licensee and the<br>proposed
          person in control in writing if the application is denied, along<br>with
          the reasons for denial, and establishes the process for requesting a<br>hearing
          to appeal the denial.<br>The bill establishes exceptions<br>to the applicability
          of its approval and application requirements with<br>respect to an acquisition
          of control, but the bill requires certain of those<br>persons specified
          by the bill to notify the commissioner of the person''s<br>grounds for not
          complying with the approval and application requirements not<br>later than
          the 15th day after the date of the acquisition of control. Subject<br>to
          specified conditions, the bill additionally makes those approval and<br>application
          requirements inapplicable to a person who has complied with and<br>received
          approval to engage in money services or was identified as a person<br>in
          control in a previous application approved by the commissioner or by a<br>state
          agency that is accredited by the Conference of State Bank Supervisors<br>and
          Money Transmitter Regulators Association for money transmission licensing<br>and
          supervision under a multistate licensing process. The bill establishes<br>that
          an individual is not considered to acquire control of a money services<br>licensee
          and is not subject to the bill''s acquisition of control provisions<br>if
          that individual becomes a key individual in the ordinary course of<br>business.<br>S.B.
          895 authorizes a person,<br>before filing an application for an approval
          to acquire control, to request in<br>writing a determination from the commissioner
          as to whether the person would<br>be considered a person in control of a
          money services licensee on<br>consummation of a proposed transaction and
          exempts a person not considered as<br>such from the approval and application
          requirements. With respect to an<br>applicant who participates in or is
          otherwise subject to a multistate<br>licensing process that includes such
          a control determination, the bill<br>provides for the commissioner''s authority
          to investigate the applicant or<br>accept the investigation results of another
          state. <br>S.B. 895 sets out the following<br>provisions regarding notice
          and information requirements for a change of key<br>individuals:<br>·requires
          a money services licensee adding or replacing a key<br>individual to provide
          notice to the commissioner not later than the 15th day<br>after the effective
          date of the individual''s appointment and the information<br>required by
          the bill for certain individuals not later than the 45th day<br>after that
          date;<br>·authorizes the commissioner to issue a notice of disapproval of<br>a
          key individual based on certain findings regarding the best interest of
          the<br>public or the customers of the licensee not later than the 90th day
          after the<br>date on which the notice of change is determined to be complete;<br>·requires
          the notice of disapproval to contain a statement of<br>the basis for disapproval
          and be sent to the licensee and the disapproved<br>individual and provides
          for the process by which the licensee may request a<br>hearing to appeal
          the disapproval;<br>·specifies that the key individual is considered approved
          if the<br>notice of change is not disapproved before the 91st day after
          the date on<br>which it was determined to be complete; and<br>·provides
          for the commissioner''s authority with respect to a<br>licensee who participates
          in or is otherwise subject to a multistate<br>licensing process that includes
          a key individual notice review and<br>disapproval process.<br>**Reporting
          and Records**<br>S.B. 895 sets out provisions<br>relating to a money transmission
          licensee''s reporting requirements as<br>follows:<br>·requires the licensee
          to submit a report of condition not later<br>than the 45th day after the
          end of the calendar quarter, or within an<br>extended time as the commissioner
          may prescribe;<br>·requires that report to include the licensee''s financial<br>information;
          nationwide and state-specific money transmission services<br>transaction
          information in every jurisdiction in the United States where the<br>licensee
          is licensed to engage in money transmission; a report on the<br>licensee''s
          permissible investments; for a fourth quarter report, transaction<br>destination
          country reporting for money received for transmission; and any<br>other
          information the commissioner reasonably requires with respect to the<br>licensee;
          <br>·authorizes the commissioner to use the NMLS for the submission<br>of
          such a report and to change or update the report requirements as necessary<br>to
          carry out the bill''s purposes and maintain consistency with NMLS reporting;<br>·requires
          the licensee to file with the commissioner by a<br>certain deadline an audited
          unconsolidated financial statement of the<br>licensee for the fiscal year,
          which must be prepared in accordance with<br>United States generally accepted
          accounting principles by a certified public<br>accountant who meets certain
          criteria, and any other information as the<br>commissioner may reasonably
          require and, with respect to the audited<br>financial statement, provides
          for additional requirements regarding a<br>certificate of opinion; and<br>·requires
          the licensee to submit a report of authorized<br>delegates not later than
          the 45th day after the end of each calendar quarter<br>containing certain
          identifying, contact, and designation information for each<br>authorized
          delegate as specified by the bill and authorizes the commissioner<br>to
          use the NMLS for the report''s submission if NMLS functionality is<br>consistent
          with that requirement.<br>S.B. 895 sets out provisions<br>relating to a
          currency exchange licensee''s reporting requirements as follows:<br>·requires
          the licensee to submit the annual report containing<br>certain financial
          information as provided by the bill that includes a<br>financial statement,
          audited or unaudited, dated as specified by the bill;<br>·requires the licensee
          to submit a quarterly interim financial<br>statement and transaction report
          that reflects the licensee''s financial<br>condition and currency exchange
          services business as of and prepared by a<br>certain date as specified by
          the bill; <br>·requires the licensee to submit any other report required
          by<br>commission rule or reasonably requested by the commissioner to determine<br>compliance
          with the bill;<br>·requires the licensee to submit those statements and
          reports<br>with the commissioner as required by the bill, by commission
          rule, or as<br>requested by the commissioner;<br>·authorizes the commissioner
          to extend the time for preparing or<br>filing such a statement or report
          on written application and for good cause shown;<br>and<br>·requires the
          licensee to file with the commissioner by a<br>certain deadline a financial
          statement, audited or unaudited, dated as<br>prescribed by the bill and
          any other information as the commissioner may<br>reasonably require and,
          for an audited financial statement, provides for<br>additional requirements
          regarding a certificate of opinion.<br>S.B. 895 requires a money<br>services
          licensee to file a report with the commissioner not later than the<br>first
          business day after the licensee has reason to know of any of the<br>following
          events:<br>·the filing of a petition by or against the licensee under<br>federal
          bankruptcy law for bankruptcy or reorganization;<br>·the filing of a petition
          by or against the licensee for<br>receivership, the commencement of any
          other judicial or administrative<br>proceeding for the licensee''s dissolution
          or reorganization, or the making of<br>a general assignment for the benefit
          of the licensee''s creditors; or<br>·the commencement of a proceeding to
          revoke or suspend the<br>licensee''s license in a state or country in which
          the licensee engages in or<br>is licensed to engage in money services business.<br>The
          bill requires a money<br>services licensee to file a report with the commissioner
          not later than the<br>third business day after the licensee has reason to
          know of the occurrence of<br>a felony charge or conviction of the following:<br>·the
          licensee or a key individual; <br>·a person in control of the licensee;
          or<br>·an authorized delegate.<br>S.B. 895 requires a money<br>services
          licensee and an authorized delegate to file all reports required by<br>federal
          currency reporting, record keeping, and suspicious activity reporting<br>requirements
          provided by the federal Bank Secrecy Act and other federal and<br>state
          laws relating to money laundering. The timely filing of such a complete<br>and
          accurate report with the appropriate federal agency is considered<br>compliant
          with the bill''s requirements. The bill requires a money services licensee<br>to
          maintain the following records, as applicable and in any form, for<br>determining
          compliance with the bill for at least five years:<br>·a general ledger posted
          at least monthly containing all asset,<br>liability, capital, income, and
          expense accounts;<br>·bank statements and bank reconciliation records;<br>·for
          a money transmission license:<br>orecords of outstanding money transmission
          obligations;<br>orecords of each outstanding money transmission obligation
          paid<br>within the five-year period and of each outstanding money transmission<br>obligation
          sold; and<br>oa list of the last known names and addresses of all of the<br>licensee''s
          authorized delegates; <br>·for a currency exchange licensee, a record of
          each currency<br>exchange transaction; and<br>·any other records the commissioner
          reasonably requires by rule.<br>The bill specifies that all<br>such records
          maintained by the licensee are open to examination by the<br>commissioner
          and authorizes the records to be maintained outside Texas so<br>long as
          they are made accessible to the commissioner not later than the seventh<br>business
          day after the commissioner sends notice in writing.<br>**Authorized**<br>**Delegates**<br>S.B.
          895 sets out provisions,<br>as follows, with respect to the relationship
          between a money transmission<br>licensee and a person the licensee designates
          as an authorized delegate to<br>engage in money transmission on behalf of
          the licensee:<br>·makes the licensee liable for the payment of all money
          or monetary<br>value received for transmission directly or by an authorized
          delegate;<br>·requires the licensee to take the following actions before<br>conducting
          business through an authorized delegate or before allowing a<br>person to
          act as such:<br>oenter into a written contract that appoints an authorized<br>delegate,
          is signed by both parties, and contains certain provisions<br>specified
          by the bill regarding each party''s duties, rights, and<br>responsibilities;<br>oadopt,
          and update as necessary, written policies and procedures<br>to ensure the
          authorized delegate complies with applicable state and federal<br>law; and<br>oconduct
          a reasonable risk-based background investigation to<br>determine whether
          the authorized delegate has complied and will likely comply<br>with that
          law;<br>·requires an authorized delegate to operate in full compliance<br>with
          the bill;<br>·establishes notice and operations requirements in the event
          of<br>the licensee''s license being suspended, revoked, surrendered, or
          expired;<br>·specifies that an authorized delegate holds in trust for the<br>licensee''s
          benefit all money net of fees received from money transmission and<br>that
          any funds or property the authorized delegate owns or controls that are<br>comingled
          with funds the authorized delegate receives from money transmission<br>are
          considered held in trust in favor of the licensee in an amount equal to<br>the
          amount of money net of fees received from money transmission; and<br>·prohibits
          an authorized delegate from using a subdelegate to<br>conduct money transmission
          on behalf of a licensee.<br>S.B. 895 requires a money<br>transmission licensee''s
          name and mailing address or telephone number to be<br>provided to the purchaser
          in connection with each money transmission<br>transaction conducted by the
          licensee directly or through an authorized<br>delegate and requires a licensee
          receiving currency or an instrument payable<br>in currency for transmission
          to comply with statutory provisions regulating<br>currency transmissions.<br>S.B.
          895 prohibits a person<br>from engaging in money transmission business on
          behalf of a person not<br>licensed or exempt from licensure under the bill''s
          provisions. The bill<br>establishes that a person who engages in unauthorized
          activity provides money<br>transmission to the same extent as if the person
          were a money transmission licensee<br>and makes the person jointly and severally
          liable with the unlicensed or<br>nonexempt person. Any business for which
          a license is required by the bill<br>that is conducted by an authorized
          delegate outside the scope of authority<br>conferred in the contract between
          the authorized delegate and the licensee is<br>unlicensed activity.<br>**Timely
          Transmission,**<br>**Refunds, and Disclosures by Money Transmission Licensee**<br>S.B.
          895 requires a money<br>transmission licensee to forward all money received
          for transmission in<br>accordance with the terms of the agreement between
          the licensee and the sender<br>unless the licensee has a reasonable belief
          or a reasonable basis to believe<br>that the sender may be a victim of fraud
          or that a crime or violation of law,<br>rule, or regulation has occurred,
          is occurring, or may occur. If the licensee<br>fails to do so, the licensee
          must respond to inquiries by the sender with the<br>reason for the failure
          unless providing a response would violate a state or<br>federal law, rule,
          or regulation.<br>S.B. 895 requires a money<br>transmission licensee to
          refund any and all money received for money<br>transmission services to
          the sender not later than the 10th day after the<br>date of receipt of the
          sender''s written request for a refund unless:<br>·the money has been forwarded
          not later than the 10th day after<br>the date on which the money was received
          for transmission;<br>·instructions have been given committing an equivalent
          amount of<br>money to the person designated by the sender not later than
          the 10th day<br>after that date;<br>·the agreement between the licensee
          and the sender instructs the<br>licensee to forward the money at a time
          that is later than the 10th day after<br>that date;<br>·the refund is requested
          for a transaction that the licensee has<br>not completed based on a reasonable
          belief or a reasonable basis to believe<br>that a crime or violation of
          law, rule, or regulation has occurred, is<br>occurring, or may occur; or<br>·the
          refund request does not enable the licensee to identify the<br>sender''s
          name and address or telephone number or, if the sender has multiple<br>outstanding
          transactions, the particular transaction to be refunded.<br>These refund
          provisions do not<br>apply to money received for money transmission that
          is subject to federal<br>regulations regarding requirements for remittance
          transfers or that is under a<br>written agreement between the licensee and
          a payee to process payments for<br>goods or services provided by the payee.
          The bill requires a licensee who,<br>under an agreement with the sender,
          has not yet forwarded funds in accordance<br>with the agreement''s terms
          to issue a refund in accordance with other<br>provisions of the bill. <br>S.B.
          895 requires a money<br>transmission licensee or authorized delegate to
          provide the sender a receipt<br>for money received for money transmission
          services that meets certain form, information,<br>and language requirements

          by phone, a receipt may be provided electronically. These<br>receipt provisions
          do not apply to the following:<br>·money received for transmission subject
          to federal regulations<br>regarding requirements for remittance transfers;<br>·money
          received for transmission that is not primarily for<br>personal, family,
          or household purposes;<br>·money received for transmission under a written
          agreement<br>between the licensee and a payee to process payments for goods
          or services<br>provided by the payee; or<br>·payroll processing services.<br>The
          bill requires a money<br>transmission licensee that provides payroll processing
          services to issue<br>reports to clients detailing client payroll obligations
          in advance of the<br>payroll funds being deducted from an account and to
          make available worker pay<br>stubs or an equivalent statement to workers.
          These requirements do not apply<br>to a licensee providing payroll processing
          services where the licensee''s<br>client designates the intended recipients
          to the licensee and is responsible<br>for providing paystubs or an equivalent
          statement.<br>**Prudential Standards**<br>S.B. 895 requires a money<br>transmission
          licensee to maintain at all times a tangible net worth in an<br>amount that
          is not less than the following:<br>·for a licensee with total assets in
          an amount not greater than<br>$100 million, the greater of $100,000 or three
          percent of the value of the<br>licensee''s total assets; <br>·for a licensee
          with total assets in an amount greater than $100<br>million and not greater
          than $1 billion, the sum of $3 million and two<br>percent of the additional
          assets in excess of $100 million; and<br>·for a licensee with total assets
          in an amount greater than $1<br>billion, the sum of $21 million and one-half
          of one percent of the<br>additional assets in excess of $1 billion.<br>Tangible
          net worth must be<br>demonstrated by the most recent audited or unaudited
          financial statements provided<br>in the initial money transmission license
          application of an applicant that is<br>a corporation, limited liability
          company, partnership, or other legal entity.<br>The bill authorizes the
          commissioner to wholly or partially exempt a money<br>transmission licensee
          from these net worth requirements for good cause shown.<br>S.B. 895 sets
          out the following<br>security provisions applicable to a money transmission

          the licensee to maintain a deposit in lieu of a bond<br>with the commissioner''s

          considered the<br>licensee''s asset or property in the event of bankruptcy,
          receivership, or a<br>claim against the licensee unrelated to the licensee''s
          obligations pursuant<br>to the license.<br>S.B. 895 sets out the following<br>provisions

          | # BILL ANALYSIS |


          |     |

          | --- |

          | S.B. 895 |

          | By: Johnson |

          | Pensions, Investments<br>& Financial Services |

          | Committee Report<br>(Unamended) |


          |     |

          | **BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE**<br>Money transmission is currently<br>regulated
          by statutes that vary widely among the different states, and the industry<br>has
          voiced concerns about the need to comply with so many different<br>requirements.
          Additionally, the current Texas statutes regulating money<br>transmission
          were originally adopted in 2005, but the business of money<br>transmission
          has significantly changed and expanded since that time. S.B. 895<br>seeks
          to update and streamline regulations to better accommodate the<br>increasing
          number of money transmitters operating within Texas and nationwide<br>by
          providing a clear set of standards that can be implemented by Texas<br>agencies
          in a consistent and coordinated manner for domestic and<br>international
          money transmitters. |

          category of offenses, or changes the eligibility of a person for community<br>supervision,
          parole, or mandatory supervision. |

          | **RULEMAKING AUTHORITY**<br>It is the committee''s opinion<br>that rulemaking
          authority is expressly granted to the Finance Commission of<br>Texas in

      content: '## Practical answer


        **Do not treat Harbor’s money transmitter licenses as assets that move to
        Mosaic in the asset purchase.** Use this closing rule:


        > **No confirmed authority means no regulated launch by Mosaic in that state.**


        The asset purchase can still close. However, Mosaic should not activate regulated
        services in the four Harbor-only states unless one of these conditions is
        met:


        1. Mosaic obtains its own license.

        2. The state approves a transfer or other license change.

        3. The regulator confirms a lawful interim structure.

        4. Harbor remains the real licensed provider under a valid transition plan.

        5. Mosaic blocks regulated functions in that state.


        The planned unified Mosaic account is important. It suggests that Mosaic,
        not Harbor, will become the service provider. If that is correct, keeping
        Harbor’s legal entity and licenses alive might not give Mosaic authority to
        operate.


        **No verified operative authority retrieved.** The collection found the CSBS
        Model Money Transmission Modernization Act and a New York regulator licensing
        page. However, no exact provision about an asset sale, license transfer, interim
        operation, or custody was available for review. Also, a model act is not proof
        of the law adopted in a specific state. The state-specific conclusions below
        remain conditional.


        ## Work needed before launch


        | Work | Why | Proposed owner | Needed by | Evidence to proceed | Fallback
        |

        |---|---|---|---|---|---|

        | Identify the four Harbor-only states | These states have the clearest authority
        gap | Licensing team | Now | Confirmed license list and covered activities
        | Block regulated functions in those states |

        | Build a matrix for every affected state | Transfer, notice, approval, and
        surrender rules can differ | State regulatory counsel | Before the closing
        conditions are final | Applicable rule, filing deadline, regulator response,
        and license status | Delay migration in the affected state |

        | Confirm the post-close service provider | The licensed entity must match
        the actual operating model | Product and deal counsel | Before customer notices
        and account design are final | Contracts, user interface, funds-flow diagram,
        and operating roles | Keep Harbor as the actual provider where permitted |

        | Review notices and approvals | An asset sale can create separate seller
        and buyer requirements | Licensing team | Before each state deadline | Filing
        receipts and required approvals or non-objections | Make approval a state
        launch condition |

        | Confirm interim operating authority | A pending application should not be
        assumed to permit operation | State regulatory counsel | Before close | Applicable
        rule or written regulator confirmation | Keep Harbor customers segregated
        or restrict transactions |

        | Review partner-bank arrangements | Bank custody does not, by itself, establish
        Mosaic’s licensing position | Payments counsel and bank relationship owner
        | Before balances move | Bank agreements, account titles, control rights,
        reconciliation design, and bank consent | Keep funds and obligations in the
        existing structure |

        | Prepare license run-off and surrender plans | Harbor may retain duties for
        balances, claims, records, and reports | Harbor compliance and deal counsel
        | Before surrender or operational shutdown | Regulator-approved plan and continued
        bonds and financial coverage | Keep Harbor licensed and operational longer
        |


        ## State notice and approval


        Do not search only for a rule called “license transfer.” Review each state
        for:


        - sale of substantially all assets;

        - change of control;

        - change in business plan;

        - change in licensed activities;

        - assignment of outstanding payment obligations;

        - change in responsible persons, locations, or agents;

        - license surrender or termination;

        - customer agreement assignment; and

        - movement of stored balances or customer funds.


        An asset purchase might fall outside a technical “change of control” rule
        because Harbor’s ownership does not change. That does not resolve the issue.
        Harbor might still need a notice or surrender approval. Mosaic might separately
        need authority before it starts the regulated activity.


        The state matrix should distinguish:


        - notice only;

        - approval before closing;

        - approval before customer migration;

        - new license required;

        - operation permitted while an application is pending;

        - regulator-approved transition available; and

        - no supported interim path.


        ## Interim operation


        Harbor could remain the licensed provider for a transition period. However,
        the structure must be real, not only contractual language.


        A supportable structure would normally need to show that:


        - Harbor remains responsible to customers.

        - Customer terms name Harbor as the provider.

        - Harbor controls the regulated activity as required.

        - Harbor’s licenses, bonds, and financial coverage remain active.

        - Customer funds and outstanding obligations remain covered.

        - Harbor can complete reports, refunds, complaints, and examinations.

        - Required records remain available.

        - Mosaic’s operational role is permitted.

        - The partner bank accepts the structure.

        - Each relevant regulator permits or accepts the structure.


        The present plan creates tension with this approach. A single Mosaic account,
        one combined balance, and full access to Mosaic products make it harder to
        show that Harbor remains the true provider.


        ## Partner-bank custody


        A partner bank account is not automatically a substitute for a money transmitter
        license. The key questions concern the complete activity and obligation flow.


        For each customer balance and transfer, document:


        1. Who receives the customer’s instruction?

        2. Who accepts the obligation to transmit or return the funds?

        3. In whose name is the bank account held?

        4. Is it a custodial or “for benefit of” account?

        5. Who can direct withdrawals?

        6. Who owns the ledger and resolves errors?

        7. Who bears loss if a transfer fails?

        8. Which entity owes the customer a refund?

        9. Which entity’s license, bond, and permissible investments cover the obligation?

        10. Does the bank agreement permit assignment, migration, or a change in the
        program manager?

        11. Is bank consent required before closing or migration?

        12. What happens to funds if Harbor, Mosaic, or the bank relationship ends?


        A bank-led model might provide a different licensing analysis if the bank
        is the actual provider and Mosaic performs only permitted services. A bank
        account that merely holds funds for Mosaic or Harbor is different. The legal
        documents, customer terms, control rights, and actual operations must all
        support the claimed model.


        Also review:


        - account segregation;

        - daily reconciliation;

        - shortfalls and reserve funding;

        - bank setoff rights;

        - liens and security interests;

        - continuity if the account is frozen;

        - treatment of pending transfers;

        - return and chargeback duties;

        - insolvency treatment;

        - customer disclosures; and

        - whether any deposit-insurance statement is accurate for the actual account
        structure.


        ## Recommended closing position


        Keep the acquisition closing separate from the regulated-service launch.


        For the four Harbor-only states, use a state launch hold unless Mosaic has
        documented authority. For overlapping states, confirm that Mosaic’s existing
        licenses cover the complete post-close product set and funds flow.


        Do not surrender Harbor’s licenses or release its bonds until the applicable
        regulators permit it and all outstanding obligations have been assigned, completed,
        or placed into an approved run-off structure.


        This investigation does not change the current recommendation. It adds one
        material point: **partner-bank custody is part of the licensing analysis,
        but custody alone does not cure an authority gap.**

    problem_analysis:

      analysis:
        schema_version: 1
        objective: Complete the Harbor asset acquisition without Mosaic conducting
          regulated money transmission without confirmed state authority or leaving
          customer funds and obligations unsupported.
        proposed_method: Move Harbor users and balances into Mosaic on day one, rely
          on Harbor licenses in four additional states, and move or maintain customer
          funds through partner-bank accounts.
        framing_note: The controlling questions are which entity performs the regulated
          activity, whether that entity has authority, what filings apply to the asset
          sale, and which entity controls and owes the customer funds. No exact operative
          state provision was available for review.
        parts:
        - key: asset-sale
          label: Asset acquisition
          description: Mosaic is buying Harbor's assets rather than Harbor's equity.
          category: relationship
          status: reported
          references:
          - kind: fact
            record_id: FACT-20260909-ed9f06
        - key: day-one-migration
          label: Day-one migration
          description: Users will move to Mosaic's app with a unified account, balance,
            and product access.
          category: activity
          status: reported
          references:
          - kind: fact
            record_id: FACT-20260909-551367
        - key: harbor-only-states
          label: Harbor-only states
          description: Mosaic plans to use or assume Harbor's licenses in four markets
            where Mosaic lacks its own reported license.
          category: constraint
          status: reported
          references:
          - kind: fact
            record_id: FACT-20260909-771ee1
        - key: provider
          label: Post-close provider
          description: The planned design suggests Mosaic will be the provider, but
            the contracts, control model, and funds flow were not supplied.
          category: actor
          status: unknown
          references: []
        - key: bank-custody
          label: Partner-bank custody
          description: The account title, beneficial ownership, control rights, bank
            consent, safeguarding treatment, and allocation of customer obligations
            are unknown.
          category: flow
          status: unknown
          references: []
        questions:
        - key: license-authority
          question: Can Harbor's license transfer or support Mosaic's post-close activity
            after the asset sale?
          why_it_matters: Mosaic may not launch regulated services without authority
            held by the entity conducting the activity.
          kind: applicability
          part_keys:
          - asset-sale
          - day-one-migration
          - harbor-only-states
          - provider
          issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045
          parent_key: null
          depends_on: []
          characterizations:
          - Entity-specific license
          - Regulator-approved transfer or amendment
          - Seller-only authority
          assessment: Do not rely on transferability without an applicable state rule,
            approval, or written regulator position.
          counterpoint: A state might permit a transfer, amendment, or approved transition,
            but no such rule was verified.
          answer_changing_fact: An applicable state provision or written regulator
            response that permits the proposed structure.
          state: conditional
          priority: decision_changing
          references: []
          next_action: research
          next_action_reason: Review the operative law and regulator procedure for
            each affected state.
        - key: filings
          question: Which seller notices, buyer applications, approvals, and surrender
            steps apply?
          why_it_matters: The required filing and its timing can control whether closing
            or customer migration may proceed.
          kind: requirement
          part_keys:
          - asset-sale
          - harbor-only-states
          issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045
          parent_key: null
          depends_on:
          - license-authority
          characterizations: []
          assessment: The answer must be determined state by state and must cover
            more than technical change-of-control rules.
          counterpoint: ''
          answer_changing_fact: The identities of the affected states and their operative
            transaction provisions.
          state: open
          priority: decision_changing
          references: []
          next_action: research
          next_action_reason: Build a state matrix with rules, deadlines, filings,
            and required approvals.
        - key: interim-operation
          question: Can Harbor remain the licensed provider while Mosaic supplies
            operational support or seeks authority?
          why_it_matters: A valid transition could maintain service, but an unsupported
            structure could leave Mosaic operating without authority.
          kind: exception
          part_keys:
          - day-one-migration
          - provider
          issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045
          parent_key: null
          depends_on:
          - license-authority
          - filings
          characterizations: []
          assessment: This path is possible only if Harbor remains the real provider
            and the relevant states permit the arrangement. The unified Mosaic account
            design may conflict with that position.
          counterpoint: A regulator-approved servicing or run-off structure may be
            available in some states.
          answer_changing_fact: Customer terms, operational control, Harbor's continued
            capacity, and written regulator positions.
          state: conditional
          priority: decision_changing
          references: []
          next_action: inspect_source

          question: Does the partner-bank structure change the licensing or safeguarding

          why_it_matters: Holding funds at a bank does not answer who accepts the

          answer_changing_fact: Account agreements, customer contracts, control rights,

          state: open

          reason: The analysis now separately tests partner-bank custody and the allocation

          answer_effect: The launch condition remains unchanged, but the state review
            must include bank contracts, account control, safeguarding, and obligation
            flows.
          references: []
        alternative_paths:
        - title: State launch hold
          proposed_change: Close the asset purchase but block regulated activity in
            states without confirmed Mosaic authority.
          benefit: Separates the corporate closing from the regulated launch.
          tradeoff: Some customers will have delayed or limited service.
          remaining_condition: Product controls must reliably identify and restrict
            affected customers.
          question_keys:
          - license-authority
          - filings
        - title: Harbor transition or run-off
          proposed_change: Keep Harbor as the actual licensed provider for a limited
            period.
          benefit: May preserve service if regulators and the partner bank accept
            the structure.
          tradeoff: Harbor must remain licensed, bonded, funded, operational, and
            responsible.
          remaining_condition: The contracts, operations, funds flow, and state rules
            must support Harbor as the true provider.
          question_keys:
          - interim-operation
          - custody
        - title: Bank-led structure
          proposed_change: Make the partner bank the actual provider while Mosaic
            supplies permitted services.
          benefit: Could change the state licensing analysis if the structure is legally
            effective.
          tradeoff: Requires major contract, product, control, disclosure, and compliance
            changes.
          remaining_condition: The bank must accept the role, and applicable state
            law must support the resulting allocation of activities.
          question_keys:
          - custody
          - license-authority
        integrated_answer: Harbor's licenses should not be treated as automatically
          transferable in the asset sale. Mosaic should launch regulated services
          only under its own confirmed authority or a documented state-approved transition.
          Partner-bank custody must be reviewed, but a bank account alone does not
          establish authority. If approvals are not ready, hold the affected state
          launch or maintain a genuine Harbor run-off structure where permitted.
        next_step: Identify the four Harbor-only states and complete one matrix covering
          license authority, transaction filings, interim operation, bank custody,
          outstanding obligations, and license surrender.

      Search Terms Search Financial Services Blog Analysis and commentary on financial
      services law, regulation, and business OCC Confirms National Bank Act Preempts
      State Money Transmitter Licensing for Fidelity Digital Assets By Keith J. Barnett
      , Ethan G. Ostroff , James Stevens & Carlin McCrory on June 11, 2026 Posted
      in Bank Regulatory On May 12, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
      (OCC) issued a significant interpretive letter confirming that Fidelity Digital
      Assets, National Association (the recently converted national trust bank formerly
      known as Fidelity Digital Assets Service, LLC) is not required to hold state
      money transmitter licenses to conduct its federally authorized activities. The
      OCC concluded that the National Bank Act preempts any state money transmitter
      licensing requirement as applied to a national bank. Until December 12, 2025,
      Fidelity Digital Assets operated as a New York-chartered limited liability trust
      company and held money tran

          on June 11, 2026 Posted in Bank Regulatory On May 12, the Office of the

          confirming that Fidelity Digital Assets, National Association (the recently
          converted national trust bank formerly known as Fidelity Digital Assets
          Service, LLC) is not required to hold state money transmitter licenses to
          conduct its federally authorized activities. The OCC concluded that the
          National Bank Act preempts any state money transmitter licensing requirement
